Tucked in the heart of the market, this humble spot is where locals actually go.

Karak tea is the star. Arabic coffee and orange juice are equally good. Tuna Chapatis is really tasteful. Prices are unbelievably reasonable for the quality.

Outdoor seating filled with locals in traditional dress creates an atmosphere no tourist attraction can replicate. Takeaway is quick and efficient.

Service is acceptable though always busy especially starts at evening, get crowded with long queues. Better come early or be prepared to share a table.

Affordable, authentic, and unpretentious. One cup of Karak here tells you more about Doha than a whole day of sightseeing.

A true gem in Doha 🇶🇦

Al Naama Cafe offers such a pleasant and authentic traditional atmosphere, with cozy seating that really lets you slow down and enjoy the moment. Even in the morning heat, the fans keep things comfortable, making it a great spot to start your day.

The staff are incredibly friendly, which adds to the welcoming vibe. My go-to order is the chapati with eggs and cheese, and sometimes I switch it up with the chapati cheese and honey — both are delicious. The karak tea is fantastic, and if you haven’t tried it with ginger (just ask!), it’s absolutely worth it.

On top of everything, the prices are extremely affordable. A must-visit if you’re in Doha and want a genuine local experience.

A great local spot inside Souq Waqif if you want to experience a casual Qatari-style hangout.

We came here to enjoy karak tea with chapati, and it was simple but very satisfying. It really feels like the kind of place where locals come to relax, chat, and enjoy a quick bite.

The seating area is quite unique, with large colorful benches where people sit together, giving the place a lively and authentic atmosphere. It’s a nice way to experience the local vibe and culture while spending time in the souq.

A great stop if you want something simple, local, and atmospheric.

This eatery seems to be a favourite among the locals. It is frequently crowded, so be prepared to share a table with other diners if you visit during peak hours. The chapati here is great.

The one notable downside to keep in mind is the moderate amount of flies buzzing around the seating area, which can be quite distracting and takes away from the overall comfort of the meal.
